Chapter 6: Integrating the Jobs Mindset Across the Organization
So, we've talked about understanding and designing for real customer jobs. Now, let’s take it a step further—how do you actually make this mindset part of your whole organization?
It’s not enough for just the innovation team to get it. Every department—whether it's marketing, operations, or even HR—should be on the same page, working toward one shared goal: helping customers make real progress.
How can you bring everyone along?
First off, start sharing customer job stories throughout your company. Use them in meetings, planning sessions, or even quick team huddles. These stories aren't just numbers—they remind us there are real people behind every data point, and they help keep teams focused on empathy.
Next, look at your internal processes. Ask yourself, "Are we actually prioritizing the customer's job?" Things like product roadmaps, service protocols, or even the way you hire people—these can all be re-examined through the lens of customer progress.
You might also want to shake up how teams work together. Instead of organizing around product lines or business units, try forming teams around specific customer jobs. This kind of cross-functional collaboration breaks down silos and helps everyone feel part of the same mission.
Let’s make this real with an example.
Imagine a financial services company. Traditionally, they might have separate teams for loans, savings, and investments. But what if, instead, they focused on jobs like, "help me feel secure about my retirement," or, "help me manage unexpected expenses"? Suddenly, the solutions become much more holistic—and a lot more meaningful for customers.
Of course, bringing this mindset to life isn’t a one-and-done deal. It’s an ongoing journey. Leaders need to show curiosity, humility, and be willing to challenge the usual way of doing things. And as the market or technology shifts, keep going back to those customer jobs. That’s how you stay responsive, resilient, and always centered on what really matters.
